mysterymodel: Opinionated Workflow for Clinical Prediction Models

Source: R/mysterymodel-package.R
mysterymodel-package.Rd

An orchestration layer for clinical prediction modelling. Established engines do the statistics: 'rms' for regression, internal validation, calibration and nomograms, the 'easystats' packages for diagnostics and interpretation, and 'tidymodels' for resampling and model comparison. This package supplies the workflow holding them together and the methodological safeguards that keep a published model honest. It makes no model-selection decision on the analyst's behalf and hides none.

Details

An orchestration layer, not an estimator. rms fits the regression, resamples it and draws the nomogram; pmsampsize answers the sample-size question; pROC supplies the interval on the c-statistic. What this package adds is the workflow holding them together and the disclosures that keep a published model honest.

The order things happen in

Each step reads the object the one before it returned, so no step has to guess and no two steps can quietly disagree about the cohort.

  1. mm_project() records the analysis plan and refuses combinations that cannot be meant. Nothing is fitted.

  2. mm_clean() applies eligibility rules and returns a ledger that reconciles: rows in equals rows out plus every exclusion, or it errors.

  3. mm_eda() describes the cohort with the denominator each percentage is taken over and the missing count beside it.

  4. mm_model() fits with rms::lrm(), decides the modelling rows once, scans for a predictor that carries the outcome, and reports whether the sample supports the parameters spent.

  5. mm_validate() returns one row per basis.

  6. mm_predict() scores new rows against the schema recorded at fit time.

  7. mm_nomogram() draws the nomogram and proves it agrees with mm_predict() before it will return one.

mm_synthetic_cohort() generates a cohort with known truth, which is what every example and article here runs on: the public repository carries no patient data.

What the package will not do quietly

The recurring decision is that a number which cannot be what it claims to be is refused or disclosed, never corrected into something plausible. A silent correction produces a figure a reader will believe.

  • A predictor that reproduces the outcome is refused, because a model given its own outcome reports near-perfect discrimination, which reads as success. Perfect separation that is not duplication is reported instead, because in a small cohort it can be real.

  • Apparent, bootstrap-corrected and held-out performance are separate rows with separate notes. Apparent calibration is withheld, because scoring an unpenalized fit on its own rows forces the intercept to zero and the slope to one.

  • A c-statistic's interval names its method and the event and non-event counts it rests on. One that cannot be computed is NA with the reason; one of zero width says so rather than reading as precision.

  • Rows dropped for incompleteness are counted, attributed to the variable that cost them, and reported as a complete-case assumption rather than a finding.

  • The fitted model carries no copy of the cohort, so a saved model cannot carry patient identifiers somewhere the data was never meant to go.

Where the reasoning is written down

inst/decisions.md holds the decision log, one record per settled question, each with the evidence behind it. inst/capability-matrix.md records which helpers in the surrounding ecosystem actually work on an rms fit, and is regenerated by data-raw/capability_spike.R.

See also

The articles, in reading order: vignette("mysterymodel") for the whole pipeline, vignette("validation") for which number to report, vignette("nomogram") for reading one back, and vignette("worked-example") for an awkward cohort and four competing plans.
